slides.headline: Kicks, throws and a cranky lower back?
slides.sub: How clinical Pilates can support your martial arts training.

slides.title: What martial arts ask for
slides.body: High kicks, sprawls, takedowns and quick pivots need hip mobility, trunk control and strength in awkward positions. Many training niggles show up where one of these runs short.

slides.title: Control at end range
slides.body: Exercises like leg circles and side-lying leg series build strength through big hip ranges. That can help your kicks feel smoother and more controlled, not just higher.

slides.title: Rotation with a steady trunk
slides.body: Punches and throws rely on turning through the mid-back while the trunk stays organised. Reformer rotation and spine twist work train this pattern at a controlled speed.

slides.title: Balance on one leg
slides.body: Single-leg work on the reformer and standing leg series builds the balance you need for kicks, switches and pivots. Slow practice here often carries over to faster drills.

slides.title: Pain that needs a check
slides.body: Deep groin or hip pain, back pain spreading into the leg, or a shoulder that feels loose after a throw is worth a physio assessment before loading it further.

slides.headline: Train with more control
slides.body: Our Pilates team designs sessions around your martial art, with exercises for your hips, trunk and balance on one leg. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
BJJ, karate, Muay Thai or taekwondo? Your hips and trunk do a lot of quiet work. 🥋

Kicks, sprawls and throws ask for strength at the end of your range, rotation through the mid-back and solid balance on one leg. Clinical Pilates can help build each of these at a controlled pace, which often carries over to faster training.

Think leg circles and side-lying work for hip control, reformer rotation for your mid-back, and single-leg work for pivots. Deep groin pain, back pain spreading into the leg or a shoulder that feels loose after a throw is worth a physio assessment first.
